english: Do you know, mother, the sign of the cloud? I know it from the smoke. When smoke does not go down to the earth, rain comes. When it rises up, there will be frost. Smoke did not go down on this day. Now cover the grain with hides. I cover it. Daughter, you are wise.

Herdsman, shall we cross the mountain? No one crosses the mountain in winter. Deep snow lies on the paths. My brother waits for me there. Stay with us. The snow melts in the heat and then you cross. Are the paths by the lake good? They are long, and wolves walk on them.
uncertain: póntoh₁s ... h₁wésus: accusative plural where a predicate nominative is expected; no verb
liméni h₂énti unclear ('in the lake'/'near the lake')

english: What does the snow bring? She, the sky's water (?). It, in winter, becomes hard and white and sinks to the earth. What is the soft one? The soft one leaves the house and the children. You drove there and left (something) to the snow. I leave; my feet are cold. Now sleep.
uncertain: séh₂ diwés wódr̥ 'she/that is the water of the sky' — gender mismatch séh₂ vs neuter wódr̥?

english: Brother, did you see that star? I saw it. Now it shone at once. When it rises at dawn, the year turns. Is spring coming now? Spring is coming, and we will lead the bullocks to the mountain. Now let us sleep. The night is long. Sit. I wake at dawn(?).
uncertain: h₁óngʷolh₁e 'at the fire/hearth?' — perhaps 'by the fire'

english: What did you hear, the thunder? That is Perkwunos's wagon. Perkwunos yokes his own wagon in the clouds. Does he thunder? He does not thunder; he brings us the rain-cloud. The grain grows and the cows will be fat. Now I am glad. Let us praise Perkwunos.
uncertain: h₁éy ne gʰrémeti contradicts first line? perhaps 'he will not thunder (strike)'

english: Brother, the thunder thunders. I am afraid. Why do you fear the thunder? It is far(?). It is not far. Perkwunos strikes (us) — strikes the rock(?) for us. Few, sister, tremble. Sit with me. The thunder does not see you inside. I sit. Do not laugh. I do not laugh.
uncertain: pérkʷum nos gʷʰént: pérkʷum 'oak/rock'? 'it struck the oak for us'
péh₂ura read as 'few' but maybe 'the fire'
